title: onboardMssp provisions the MSSP organization and its framework pool without an owner when ownerMode resolves to "none"
description: admin.controller.js onboardMssp: legacy inviteOwner:false maps to ownerMode 'none' (line 348); MsspProvider is created with status:'provisioning' and stays there since no ownerAccess is produced (line 402); MsspFrameworkLicense rows are inserted active regardless of owner state.
steps: POST /admin/tenant-management/mssps with organization + frameworks:["iso27001"] and inviteOwner:false
expectedResult: Response is 201 with status:"provisioning", ownerInvitationId:null, frameworkCount:1; provisioning.inviteOrgUser is never called; exactly one active MsspProvider (status="provisioning") and one active MsspFrameworkLicense exist.

title: onboardMssp with ownerMode="invite" creates an active provider and an mssp_owner invitation in one call
description: admin.controller.js onboardMssp invite branch (lines 382-392): provisioning.inviteOrgUser is called with roleKey=MSSP_OWNER, type=mssp_owner; provider.status flips to "active" once ownerAccess exists (line 402-403).
steps: POST /admin/tenant-management/mssps with organization, owner, frameworks, ownerMode:"invite"
expectedResult: Response status:"active", ownerMode:"invite", ownerUserId and ownerInvitationId populated; MsspProvider.status is "active" in the database.

title: onboardMssp with ownerMode="add" creates an active provider and a Keycloak owner with a one-time temporary password
description: admin.controller.js onboardMssp add branch (lines 393-401) calls createOrgUserWithTemporaryPassword with roleKey=MSSP_OWNER; response includes temporaryPassword once, persisted operation/audit records do not.
steps: POST /admin/tenant-management/mssps with organization, owner, frameworks, ownerMode:"add"
expectedResult: Response status:"active", ownerMode:"add", temporaryPassword present in the HTTP body only; ProvisioningOperation.result.temporaryPassword and MsspAuditEvent "mssp.onboarded".after.temporaryPassword are both undefined.

title: provisionMsspOwner activates a provision-only MSSP by adding its first owner later
description: admin.controller.js provisionMsspOwner: if provider.status==='provisioning' it flips to 'active' once the owner is created/invited (lines 547-551) — completing the deferred-owner path started by onboardMssp with ownerMode 'none'.
preconditions: An MsspProvider exists with status "provisioning" and no owner yet
expectedResult: Response 201 with providerStatus:"active" and the new invitationId; the MsspProvider document's status is now "active".

title: createClient (ownerMode="invite") activates the relationship and records a "mssp.client.created" audit event with the correct payload
description: mssp.controller.js createClient: relationship starts "provisioning" (line 152) and is flipped to "active" after all projects are created (line 199); MsspAuditEvent "mssp.client.created" (lines 217-221) records after:{projectCount, ownerMode} and correlationId equal to the ProvisioningOperation id.
steps: POST /mssp/clients with ownerMode:"invite" and one project
expectedResult: MsspClientRelationship.status is "active"; exactly one MsspAuditEvent with action "mssp.client.created" exists, with after.ownerMode==="invite" and after.projectCount===1, and correlationId equal to the ProvisioningOperation's _id.

title: createClient (ownerMode="add") never persists the plaintext temporary password to the operation or audit record
description: mssp.controller.js createClient add branch; verified end to end against real MongoDB documents.
steps: POST /mssp/clients with ownerMode:"add" and one project
expectedResult: Response includes temporaryPassword once; the persisted ProvisioningOperation("mssp_client_onboarding").result.temporaryPassword is undefined, and MsspAuditEvent("mssp.client.created").after.temporaryPassword is undefined while after.ownerMode is "add".

title: createClient (ownerMode="provider_managed") sets accessModel=provider_managed and creates no duplicate client-side user
description: mssp.controller.js createClient: ownerAccess is null for provider_managed (line 159); MsspClientRelationship.accessModel is set from ownerMode at creation (line 153); createPendingProject receives ownerUserId:null.
steps: POST /mssp/clients with ownerMode:"provider_managed", owner.email reused from the provider's own auditor
expectedResult: Response has ownerUserId:null, ownerInvitationId:null, temporaryPassword:null, credentialDelivery:"mssp_relationship"; inviteOrgUser and createOrgUserWithTemporaryPassword are never called; the persisted MsspClientRelationship has accessModel="provider_managed" and status="active".

title: inviteClientUser rejects a projectIds list containing a project that does not belong to the target client organization
description: mssp.controller.js inviteClientUser (lines 306-309): when projectIds is non-empty, it counts matching Project documents scoped to org._id and compares against the requested set size, throwing AppError.badRequest("One or more projects do not belong to this client") on any mismatch.
preconditions: Managed client A with project P1; a different organization's project P2 exists
expectedResult: The call is rejected with 400 "One or more projects do not belong to this client"; no user, invitation, or ProjectMember row is created.

title: inviteClientUser adds a managed-client user in "add" mode with a one-time temporary password and correct audit action
description: mssp.controller.js inviteClientUser add branch and MsspAuditEvent "mssp.client_user.added".
expectedResult: Response includes temporaryPassword and credentialDelivery="keycloak_first_login_prompt", invitation:null; the MsspAuditEvent "mssp.client_user.added".after.temporaryPassword is undefined.

title: inviteTeamMember rejects any roleKey outside the four MSSP provider roles
description: mssp.controller.js inviteTeamMember (lines 434-436): roleKey must be one of MSSP_OWNER/MSSP_OPERATOR/MSSP_BILLING_VIEWER/MSSP_USER_ADMIN or the call is rejected with 400 'Invalid MSSP role' — this stops a provider from granting a customer-side or platform role to its own team.
expectedResult: The call is rejected with 400 "Invalid MSSP role"; no user or invitation is created.

title: createPendingProject rejects a framework selection that exceeds the chosen plan's configured framework limit
description: tenant-provisioning.service.js createPendingProject (lines 452-462) calls frameworkEntitlement.assertFrameworkLimit with the plan's frameworkLimitForPlan(); a project requesting more distinct frameworks than the plan allows must be rejected server-side even if the client-panel's own pre-submit check (clients/new/page.jsx setProjectFrameworks) were somehow bypassed.
steps: Call createPendingProject (or POST /mssp/clients/:id/projects) with 2 frameworks against a plan whose frameworkLimit is 1
expectedResult: The call throws/returns a framework-limit error and no Project, SubscriptionInstance, or ClientFramework row is created.

title: createPendingProject activates every selected paid-plan framework immediately, independent of payment/billing state
description: tenant-provisioning.service.js createPendingProject + activateProjectFrameworks: for an mssp_client org on a project-scoped plan, every selected framework becomes an active ClientFramework row and the SubscriptionInstance is 'active' with no legacy plan cap or payment gate blocking activation.
preconditions: mssp_client org, project-scoped plan with frameworkLimit=-1, two active ComplianceFrameworks
steps: Call createPendingProject with both frameworks selected
expectedResult: The resulting SubscriptionInstance.status is "active" and exactly 2 ClientFramework rows exist with status "active" for that project.

title: replaceFrameworkCatalog (admin) upserts newly desired frameworks as active and revokes ones removed from the desired set
description: admin.controller.js replaceFrameworkCatalog (lines 574-603): frameworks present in req.body.frameworks are upserted to status "active"; existing MsspFrameworkLicense rows whose frameworkId is not in the desired set are updated to status "revoked" with revocationEffectiveAt, never deleted — preserving the historical record for already-provisioned client data.
preconditions: Provider currently licensed for ISO 27001 and SOC 2
expectedResult: ISO 27001 remains active; SOC 2's license row now has status "revoked" and a revocationEffectiveAt timestamp (its document is not deleted); HIPAA now has an active license row; a "mssp.framework_catalog.replaced" audit event records the before/after code lists.

title: detachClient requires a non-empty reason and cannot be replayed against an already-detached relationship
description: admin.controller.js detachClient (line 632): blank/missing reason -> 400. The lookup filter status:{$ne:'detached'} (line 633) means a second detach call against the same clientOrgId after the first succeeded finds no matching relationship and returns 404, rather than silently reprocessing or double-writing the OwnershipTransfer/audit trail.
steps: POST /admin/tenant-management/clients/:clientOrgId/detach with an empty reason string
POST the same endpoint with a valid reason and succeed
POST the identical detach call again
expectedResult: Call 1 returns 400. Call 2 succeeds and returns transferId/status:"complete". Call 3 returns 404 "Managed client relationship not found" — detach is not idempotently reprocessed, and only one OwnershipTransfer/audit event exists for this client.

title: detachAllClients converts every non-detached client in one batch and stamps the provider status "deowned" with a single audit event
description: admin.controller.js detachAllClients (lines 667-686): bulk MsspClientRelationship.updateMany + Organization.updateMany + a single MsspProvider status update, then one "mssp.deowned" MsspAuditEvent carrying after.detachedClientCount.
preconditions: Provider with 3 active managed clients and 1 already-detached client
expectedResult: detachedClientCount is 3 (the already-detached one is excluded); all 3 relationships are now "detached" with matching detachedBy/detachReason; all 3 organizations now have kind="direct_customer"; MsspProvider.status is "deowned"; exactly one "mssp.deowned" audit event exists with after.detachedClientCount===3.

title: routeFor() assigns a managed client's request to the platform admin queue when the relationship's requestRoutingPolicy is admin_only
description: request.service.js routeFor() (lines 41-58): route defaults to 'mssp' for an active relationship, but is forced to 'admin' whenever relationship.requestRoutingPolicy==='admin_only' or customerSelfRequestEnabled===false — this is the MSSP relationship-config field directly controlling which queue (/mssp/requests vs the platform admin queue) a request lands in.
steps: Submit a framework-add request for client C via POST /mssp/clients/C/requests, acting as the MSSP
expectedResult: The created SubscriptionRequest has route="admin" and assignedApproverType="admin"; it does NOT appear in that provider's GET /mssp/requests results filtered to reviewable items (see MSSP-SEC-013), even though the provider is the one who submitted it.
